title: stalex444/pdt-lean
abstract: Kernel-checked exact-constant results for the CHSH operator T = A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ − A₁B₁ of an arbitrary CHSH tuple (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple: self-adjoint involutions with the A's commuting with the B's). (1) The Landau identity: in any *-ring, T² = 4 + [A₀,A₁]·[B₁,B₀] — the exact, representation-independent correction to the naive T² = 8·1 (chsh_mul_self). (2) Tsirelson's bound in norm form: ‖T‖ ≤ 2√2 for every CHSH tuple in every nontrivial unital real C*-normed algebra (chsh_norm_le). (3) The classical constant, exactly: if either party's pair commutes, ‖T‖ = 2 — not merely ≤ 2 (chsh_norm_of_comm). (4) Necessity of noncommutativity: any violation ‖T‖ > 2 forces A₀A₁ ≠ A₁A₀ and B₀B₁ ≠ B₁B₀ — noncommutativity within both parties is necessary for any violation of the classical bound (noncomm_of_chsh_norm_gt_two). (5) The exact constant of M₄(ℝ): in the l2 operator norm, 2√2 is the greatest element of the set of CHSH operator norms over 4×4 real matrices — an upper bound for every tuple, attained by an explicit real-Pauli tuple (chsh_opNorm_isGreatest), so the maximal violation 2√2 is possible, not just bounded. The witness side stays compared: the explicit quadruple is verified to be a genuine CHSH tuple, its CHSH operator has eigenvalue exactly 2√2 on the explicit nonzero vector (1,0,0,1) and l2 operator norm exactly 2√2; the ordered star-ring bounds T ≤ (2√2)·1 and (commutative case) T ≤ 2 and the strict gap 2 < 2√2 complete the picture. A falsification is compared alongside: the saturating tuple's T² is not c·1 for ANY real c (chsh_sq_ne quantifies over every scalar), so the scalar-square route to the norm is closed for every scalar; the norm results here go through the C*-identity (and, for the generic bound, the Landau identity) instead.
